raw_comment:
From the graph I noticed that the heat wave has been increasing through the years. In July 17, 2023, the temperature reached 63° fahrenheit. I believe that if we continue to emit carbon dioxide at the current rate of global warming, the world will become even hotter, and in the worst case scenario, humanity will no longer be able to live on the earth.
Up until now, the government and coalitions have encouraged people to walk instead of using their cars or to turn on air conditioning immediately, but from now on, I think it is necessary to set a firm limit by law. As I wasn't aware that global warming had become so bad until I saw this graph, I believe that many people are unaware of the extent to which global warming is progressing, so we need to make people aware of the bad effects and encourage each person to have a sense of urgency. To encourage each person to have a sense of urgency, I think we can consider in detail the worst case scenario that could happen due to global warming, and search for the state of islands that are now gone or about to be gone due to global warming. Although few of today's adults may be thinking deeply about this because they will not be alive in 2050, I hope that they will think about their own children who will become adults in the future and take appropriate actions with a sense of crisis that the world in which their children will live may disappear. 
I believe it is now time to start action for our future.

This graph aims to show the spike in air temperature. This spike happened during this recent summer. However, there had been a slight increase in temp since around April 14th. In the months leading up to summer, there had also been about a .3-degree increase compared to last year. Then in summer, the average temp jumped to a whole degree over 2022 and a record high since 1979.
             "Why did this happen?" I wonder. One popular and common answer these days is global warming. With the increase in global warming, it'd make sense to see an increase in temperature. However, many also believe this may have something to do with the Wildfire in Canada.
            The Canadian wildfire, left much of New York in smoke. Smoke that drifted as far down the coast as North Carolina. The date of the fire starting coincides very well with the prominent spike. And if its causing that much smoke, is it not plausible that it could cause the bump in air temperatures? 
        The only problem with this theory is that, their have been multiple wildfires and forest fires in the past and yet they dont seem to have shown any spikes. So why is this specific on so significant? It might be due to its timing being in the middle of summer. Whatever the reason may be, its very interesting that it happened. That's why Id make the headline of this graph. "Who knew such a cool event... Could be so hot!"

raw_comment:
This graph is truly frightening. It shows us the dire way in which global temperature has been changing, and 2023 is disturbingly drastic. The temperature in each year follows a similar path: a relatively low, cool temperature to start off the year,  a slow ascendance up into the hot, summer months, and an equally slow descendance down again, wrapping up the year and tying it into a neat little bow. 2023 starts off the year fairly normal. It begins the year with a temperature of around 56 degrees, same as the others. Then June hits, and temperatures soar to 62.5, the highest temperature recorded since before 1979, according to this graph. 

What comes next? It is impossible for me to believe that human activity had no impact on this sudden surge in heat, what else could cause such a catastrophic change in only a year? We have been warned: told again and again about the effects of our actions, our insistence to continue drilling, to continue polluting the place we call home, and while we pretend to care, we do nothing. It is as if we are slowly falling into an apocalypse.  How are we going to recover? Are we going to adjust, find some miraculous way to save ourselves and live out the rest of our existence surviving upon the corpse of a once vivid, breathing planet, now an ashen ghost of a life? Or will we die a slow death, blissfully unaware of our dwindling state of life until it is all too late? As much as we try to ignore it all, someday it is sure to catch up to us.

raw_comment:
Record High Global Surface Temperature Shows Alarming Effects of Climate Change.

I noticed that the global average surface temperature has relatively maintained a median temperature, every year, during every season because of the way that they "clump"... obviously with the exception of this year where the spike in July can be seen.  I also noticed that after the stark spike in July the temperature has greatly digressed but it still stands as an outlier even after the fact.  I wonder if this pattern or increasingly regular high temperatures will continue next year and how the unknown effects of climate change amidst the thousands of known will continue to change lives.  More so, I wonder the effect these high temperatures will have on this year.  Will we have contrasting bitter cold winters with the increased evaporated water in the atmosphere and the change in arctic oscillation or will we have warmer winters?  I live on the east coast and my community and I are no strangers to hurricanes.   Hotter temperatures affect the rainfall and intensity of the hurricanes and can make them much more devastating.   With the increase in temperatures in recent years communities along the east coast have been dealing with increasingly worse storms more often causing a wide array of harmful effects that go deeper than physical damage.  I wonder how they will continue to affect my vulnerable community.

What do you notice?
I notice that there is an upward trend on this graph using data from previous years as a marginal baseline to offer context and comparison. We notice that from 1979-2021 the average temperatures within a given month appear to be higher and higher as the years progress. For example, on July 1st in the years surrounding 1979 the temperatures seemed to average at about 61 degrees in stark comparison to the 62-63 average for July 1st 2023.
What do you wonder?
I begin to wonder at what rate, if any, our temperatures are rising and how long it would possibly take for these temperatures could become dangerous for human existence. Will this alter the way we lead our lives should global warming cause irreparable damage to the Earth? Which again, ties back into this idea of how animal lives might be affected as well since we have witnessed the extinction of several animals due to global warming.
How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because the change has almost been inherent or maybe even explicit at times because as a town up North in America, we were used to seeing inches of snow every year and tolerable summer temperatures. Last year I think we got less than an inch of snow combined as well as unbearable waves of heat during July as well as September that we had not experienced as long as we lived which makes sense with such a rise in temperatures in recent years.

4) Rising Temperatures or Rising Concerns?

How We Are Ruining Ourselves

 This graph does a really great job at highlighting the problem of global warming in the world today. Why I say this is because it you look at the graph you first see that in 1979-2021, 42 years it stayed about the same and there were no major problems but once you get to 2022 you see that is was at a very high point from even the colder months to the hot months and still stayed very high in the later months that were the coldest. Then we get to the current year and it starts off normal but as the year goes on it shoots up like a rocket to about a degree higher that 2022 every month and who knows what this graph will look like at the end of the year. I really think that we need to try to prevent this before we ruin our world.
     I was in Rock Hill, SC during July 17th when it reached its all time high and I noticed how to air was a little bit darker, sort of like a red-orange color just stuck in the air and I saw on my phone a WECT notification that said something along the lines of the air is not safe, and I started to panic, I thought to myself “what is going to happen to me” but my parents reassured me that it was nothing to worry about and it wasn't a dire situation. 
     One thing I wonder about this graph is how it can go up so fast in such a short amount of time.

We must put in our effort and hope that it makes this rising trend change course and stop harming the world we all love so much.

"Highest Summer Heat EVER"

Over the course of almost fifty years the daily global surface air temperatures have risen by an average of 2-3 degrees. In fact we just had the highest temperature past July.

The increasing temperatures relate to me because it is causing it to be hard to cut the grass in July, causing our grass to get longer than usual. It relates to my community because it puts an impact on people trying to do stuff outside.  Also I see it impacting fires, by expanding and happening a lot more than usual.

"Colossal Climate Crisis"
